transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have some questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening after cataract surgery?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month after your operation.

So gentle gardening is fine, but try to avoid anything too demanding for now.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the advice! I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your care team.

However, if you need a new supply, your GP should be able to provide some more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying! Here's another one: I'm very sensitive to bright lights right now. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Yes, that's quite normal! It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside. However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or your eye is red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: Yes, that's quite normal! It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, but should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, and this should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, if your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

How long has it been since your surgery?

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been a little over a week now. Thank you for addressing my questions! I don't have any more for now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Brilliant! Just to confirm - have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and don't hesitate to get in touch if you have any concerns during your recovery.

verdict.label: fail
